title: Inspecting Raw Data
learning_outcomes: Explain inspecting raw data and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of inspecting raw data to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study inspecting raw data in the context of data cleaning and preprocessing. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Inspecting Raw Data matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Cleaning means making explicit, documented decisions about quality problems while preserving provenance and avoiding transformations that leak future information.

items.title: Dimensions and data types
items.text: Define dimensions and data types in relation to inspecting raw data; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

items.title: Column names
items.text: Work through column names using a small, synthetic example before scaling up. State what the calculation or method returns and why that result is useful.

items.title: Summary statistics
items.text: Check the edge cases for summary statistics: missing values, unusual ranges, different groups, time boundaries, or a changed input can affect the conclusion.

items.title: Sample records
items.text: Document the rule or choice for sample records so another learner can reproduce the analysis and understand its limitations.

items.title: Unexpected values
items.text: Define unexpected values in relation to inspecting raw data; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by inspecting raw data. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.run_instructions: For Python, copy the snippet into a local file and run with Python 3. This CodeLeaf block is static and does not execute inside the browser. For SQL, adapt the query to an approved local schema; the stated result is a conceptual query simulation, not a live database result.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. Duplicates should be defined by a business key, not assumed from visual similarity.

content_blocks.title: Responsible interpretation
content_blocks.text: This example is a teaching aid. It is static in the CodeLeaf lesson and is not executed in the browser. It uses small synthetic values; validate any real workflow in a separate, appropriate local environment and protect sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Cleaning means making explicit, documented decisions about quality problems while preserving provenance and avoiding transformations that leak future information. Next, connect this lesson to the linked prerequisite or following lesson. Record the method, input assumptions, observed result, and one limitation so another person can reproduce and review the work.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small synthetic example for inspecting raw data. State a question, make a prediction, trace or run an appropriate calculation, then write one finding and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: Refer accurately to the topic and its syllabus subtopics.
Record a reproducible example or a complete manual trace with an expected result.
Document at least one assumption, limitation, data-quality issue, or evaluation check.
hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
troubleshooting: Check input values, path assumptions, package versions, indentation, and units.
For SQL, use a local schema and read-only test data; this page does not provide a live database.
For package-dependent work, create an isolated environment and use the relevant official documentation.
